chunks: My father, may God be pleased with him, narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan ibn Ahmad al-Maliki narrated to us, from his father, from Ali ibn al-Mu'ammal. He said:

I met Musa ibn Ja'far, peace be upon them both, and he used to dye with red. So I said: May I be your sacrifice! This is not from the dyeing practice of your family. He said: Yes indeed, I used to dye with isatis (woad plant), but it loosened my teeth.

Indeed, when a man would embrace Islam during the time of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and his family, he would do that. And indeed, the Commander of the Believers, peace be upon him, dyed with yellow, and the news reached the Prophet, may God bless him and his family, and he said: "Islam." Then he dyed with red, and the news reached the Prophet, may God bless him and his family, and he said: "Islam and faith." Then he dyed with black, and the news reached the Prophet, may God bless him and his family, and he said: "Islam, faith, and light."

key_terms.إِسْلَام: Islam, meaning submission to God -- the first level of spiritual attainment
key_terms.إِيمَان: Iman (faith), a deeper inner conviction beyond outward submission
key_terms.خِضَاب: Dyeing (of hair or beard), a practice with spiritual and cultural significance in Islamic tradition
key_terms.نُور: Nur (light), representing the highest spiritual illumination
key_terms.وَسْمَة: Isatis or woad, a plant used to produce dark blue/black dye, known to have harsh chemical properties

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet Muhammad say about the spiritual significance of different hair dyeing colors in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Amali of Shaykh al-Saduq records a conversation between Ali ibn al-Mu'ammal and Imam Musa ibn Ja'far al-Kadhim (the seventh Imam) about the practice of dyeing hair/beard. The Imam explains that he switched from isatis (woad) to red dye due to dental issues, and then relates the prophetic tradition about dyeing practices: when the Commander of the Believers (Imam Ali) dyed yellow, the Prophet called it "Islam"; when he dyed red, it was "Islam and faith"; and when he dyed black, it was "Islam, faith, and light" -- associating progressively deeper spiritual stations with each color.

en.bilal-muhammad: My father (ra) narrated to us. He said: Al-Hasan b. Ahmad al-Maliki narrated to us from his father from `Ali b. al-Mu’ammal. He said:

I met Musa b. Ja`far (as) and he used to dye with red. So, I said: May I be your sacrifice! This is not from the dye of your family. So, he said: Yes, I used to dye with isatis, but it began hurting my teeth.

When a man would convert to Islam during the time of the Messenger of Allah (s), he would do that. Once, Amir al-Mu’minin (as) dyed with yellow, and he told the Prophet (s) that, and he said: “Islam.” So, he dyed with red, and he told the Prophet (s) that, and he said: “Islam and faith.” So, he dyed with black, and he told the Prophet (s) that, and he said: “Islam, faith, and light.”
